author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Senator Rick Scott urges DOT to address refund policy impacting travel agencies
text:
Senator Rick Scott urges DOT to address refund policy impacting travel agencies
U.S. Senator Rick Scott sent a letter on Sep. 2 to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy urging changes to a federal policy that he said places an unfair financial burden on travel agents, many of whom are small business owners in Florida.
Currently, regulations require travel agents to refund customers within seven days after a qualified flight cancellation or delay, while airlines are not subject to the same deadline. As a result, agents must pay refunds out of pocket and then wait for reimbursement from airlines, which may take months. In his letter, Scott requested that the Department of Transportation hold airlines equally accountable by setting deadlines for them to return funds so that small businesses are not left financially exposed.
Scott wrote, “Travel agencies and advisors operate on slim margins, and many simply cannot afford to front refunds to their customers, particularly for group bookings worth tens of thousands of dollars, before the airline has returned the money. These small businesses are being held financially accountable for a timeline they do not control, while the airlines that actually hold the funds face no enforceable deadline. Many of these small businesses may go out of business if nothing is done. Small businesses are the backbone of the American economy and travel advisors and agencies play a critical role in our tourism industry.”
The senator's letter highlighted concerns with Department rules issued in April 2024 requiring "merchants of record"—often travel agencies—to issue timely refunds even though they do not retain customer funds after ticket purchase. The August 2024 rule requires airlines only to "promptly" return those funds but does not define what constitutes promptness or set any specific deadline.
Scott asked Secretary Duffy and the Department either to establish clear deadlines for airline reimbursements or align agency refund obligations with receipt of funds from carriers: “Consumers deserve timely refunds, but that obligation should rest with the party holding the money, not with small businesses left waiting on the airlines.”
Scott champions fiscal responsibility and policies supporting families and small businesses; he served in the U.S. Navy aboard USS Glover after high school; he won election as Florida’s U.S. Senator; earned degrees from University of Missouri-Kansas City and Southern Methodist University; serves on several Senate committees including Armed Services; and enjoys time with his wife Ann—their high school sweetheart marriage—and family members, according to the official website.

In his letter, Scott requested that the Department of Transportation hold airlines equally accountable by setting deadlines for them to return funds so that small businesses are not left financially exposed.
